evidence.claim: The congress adopted a revised Party Constitution and called on the whole Party, the military, and the Chinese people to rally closely around the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core.
evidence.title: 20th CPC National Congress concludes in Beijing, Xi Jinping presides over closing session and delivers important speech
evidence.excerpt: The congress adopted a revised Party Constitution and called on the whole Party, the military, and the Chinese people to rally closely around the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core.
evidence.source_locator: Opening report paragraphs and the closing-session summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous official congress text; direct statement of party-state consolidation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Xi because he presided over the closing session and the text centers his core position.
contrary_evidence: This is intra-party consolidation, not public democratic contestability.

evidence.claim: Xi secured a precedent-breaking third term and installed a top governing body stacked with loyalists.
evidence.title: China's Xi clinches third term, packs leadership with loyalists
evidence.excerpt: Xi secured a precedent-breaking third term and installed a top governing body stacked with loyalists.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a high-salience party leadership outcome, contemporaneous and widely corroborated.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Xi as the incumbent who benefited from and shaped the leadership outcome.
contrary_evidence: This reports a party appointment process, not an open election.

evidence.claim: Hu Jintao was unexpectedly escorted out of the 20th Party Congress closing ceremony while the congress unanimously advanced Xi's political vision.
evidence.title: Chinese ex-President Hu Jintao escorted out of party congress
evidence.excerpt: Hu Jintao was unexpectedly escorted out of the 20th Party Congress closing ceremony while the congress unanimously advanced Xi's political vision.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters contemporaneous coverage of a symbolic power-display event at the party congress.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly associated with Xi because the event occurred at his congress and underscored his dominance.
contrary_evidence: The exact reason for Hu's removal was not publicly explained.

evidence.claim: Chinese property developers faced $117 billion of debt maturing in 2022 and an unprecedented liquidity squeeze after Beijing's campaign to rein in borrowing in the sector.
evidence.title: Chinese property developers face big debt maturities in 2022
evidence.excerpt: Chinese property developers faced $117 billion of debt maturing in 2022 and an unprecedented liquidity squeeze after Beijing's campaign to rein in borrowing in the sector.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting with concrete sector metrics and direct policy context.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and describes the inherited property-sector problem Xi had to manage.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution is indirect but relevant because the tightening campaign and its consequences arose under Xi's national policy setting.
contrary_evidence: This does not by itself show whether the crackdown was prudent or reckless.

evidence.claim: Chinese regulators stepped in to help local governments guarantee delivery of unfinished homes after mortgage-payment boycotts spread, reflecting a targeted rescue response to property-sector unrest.
evidence.title: China vows timely home deliveries in wake of property protests
evidence.excerpt: Chinese regulators stepped in to help local governments guarantee delivery of unfinished homes after mortgage-payment boycotts spread, reflecting a targeted rescue response to property-sector unrest.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reported a contemporaneous, policy-specific intervention with clear sectoral consequences.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Xi because the intervention was part of the national policy response under his leadership, though the immediate action came through regulators.
contrary_evidence: The rescue response mitigated harm but also confirms the severity of the underlying property stress.

evidence.claim: Reuters described a revolt by homebuyers over unfinished projects as forcing a shakeout among cash-starved developers who had relied on apartment pre-sales.
evidence.title: Analysis: China's mortgage boycott spurs shakeout among strapped developers
evidence.excerpt: Reuters described a revolt by homebuyers over unfinished projects as forcing a shakeout among cash-starved developers who had relied on apartment pre-sales.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters analysis based on contemporaneous market developments and a specific mechanism of distress.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant because the phenomenon reflected the policy and regulatory environment under Xi's rule.
contrary_evidence: This is an analysis piece, not a government finding or formal audit.

evidence.claim: Reuters said Chinese developers sharply cut property investment in July 2022 and new construction starts suffered their biggest fall in nearly a decade.
evidence.title: Chinese developers in 'survival mode' slash property investment
evidence.excerpt: Reuters said Chinese developers sharply cut property investment in July 2022 and new construction starts suffered their biggest fall in nearly a decade.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting using official and market data on a major growth sector.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Xi because the property downturn unfolded under his national policy regime and affected the macro trajectory he controlled.
contrary_evidence: The article reports sector stress; it does not prove Xi's policy choices were the sole cause.

evidence.claim: Reuters identified Li Qiang as a close Xi ally and He Lifeng as a longtime ally who headed the state planning commission, while reformers such as Hu Chunhua were expected to step down.
evidence.title: Factbox-China's 20th Communist Party Congress: who could be in Xi's new team?
evidence.excerpt: Reuters identified Li Qiang as a close Xi ally and He Lifeng as a longtime ally who headed the state planning commission, while reformers such as Hu Chunhua were expected to step down.
evidence.source_locator: Factbox entries for Li Qiang, He Lifeng, and Hu Chunhua
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters factbox on imminent elite appointments with direct relevance to economic policymaking personnel.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Xi because these were the personnel choices surrounding his consolidation of economic authority.
contrary_evidence: Expected promotions are not the same as proven economic competence.

evidence.claim: Xi secured a precedent-breaking third term and introduced a top governing body stacked with loyalists, cementing his power over the party.
evidence.title: China's Xi clinches third term, packs leadership with loyalists
evidence.excerpt: Xi secured a precedent-breaking third term and introduced a top governing body stacked with loyalists, cementing his power over the party.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters contemporaneous report on the outcome of the Party Congress.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Xi as the beneficiary and center of the leadership reshuffle.
contrary_evidence: This is a political power fact, not itself an economic performance measure.

evidence.claim: The Party Constitution was amended to add common prosperity, a domestic-economy-centered development pattern, and language calling for higher-quality, more equitable, sustainable, and secure economic development.
evidence.title: Full text of resolution on Party Constitution amendment
evidence.excerpt: The Party Constitution was amended to add common prosperity, a domestic-economy-centered development pattern, and language calling for higher-quality, more equitable, sustainable, and secure economic development.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official Party Congress text showing declared economic priorities and Xi-centered ideological direction.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant because this was Xi's congress and the amended constitution reflects his leadership agenda.
contrary_evidence: Declared goals are not the same as implemented outcomes.

evidence.claim: Fixed-asset investment rose 5.1 percent in 2022, with infrastructure up 9.4 percent, manufacturing up 9.1 percent, high-tech manufacturing and services reported as strong, health and social work up 26.1 percent, private investment up only 0.9 percent, and property development down 10.0 percent.
evidence.title: Investment in Fixed Assets from January to December 2022
evidence.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China
evidence.excerpt: Fixed-asset investment rose 5.1 percent in 2022, with infrastructure up 9.4 percent, manufacturing up 9.1 percent, high-tech manufacturing and services reported as strong, health and social work up 26.1 percent, private investment up only 0.9 percent, and property development down 10.0 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official investment dataset with sectoral detail directly relevant to policy mix and trajectory.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Xi because the investment mix reflects the national economic strategy and constraints under his leadership.
contrary_evidence: Strong state-led and high-tech investment coexisted with very weak private investment and a property slump.

evidence.claim: Real estate development investment fell 10.0 percent in 2022; housing starts fell 39.4 percent; sales area fell 24.3 percent; and funding for developers fell 25.9 percent.
evidence.title: National Real Estate Development and Sales in 2022
evidence.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China
evidence.excerpt: Real estate development investment fell 10.0 percent in 2022; housing starts fell 39.4 percent; sales area fell 24.3 percent; and funding for developers fell 25.9 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official sector statistics with direct relevance to the property crisis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Xi because the property downturn was a central macroeconomic problem under his rule and policy setting.
contrary_evidence: The report measures the downturn; it does not itself assign blame or assess the policy mix's necessity.

evidence.claim: The NBS said high-tech manufacturing investment rose 22.2 percent, high-tech services 12.1 percent, infrastructure 9.4 percent, health and social work 26.1 percent, and property development investment fell 10 percent in 2022.
evidence.title: China's fixed-asset investment maintains stable growth in 2022
evidence.excerpt: The NBS said high-tech manufacturing investment rose 22.2 percent, high-tech services 12.1 percent, infrastructure 9.4 percent, health and social work 26.1 percent, and property development investment fell 10 percent in 2022.
evidence.source_locator: Body text, paragraphs on sectoral investment
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government summary of the annual investment composition and policy support measures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Xi because it shows what the state prioritized during his 2022 rule.
contrary_evidence: The same source shows property weakness and only marginal private-investment growth.

evidence.claim: China created 12.06 million new urban jobs in 2022, but the 16-24 unemployment rate reached 16.7 percent in December and NBS said young people faced greater hiring difficulty.
evidence.title: China's job market remains stable in 2022
evidence.excerpt: China created 12.06 million new urban jobs in 2022, but the 16-24 unemployment rate reached 16.7 percent in December and NBS said young people faced greater hiring difficulty.
evidence.source_locator: Body paragraphs on employment and youth unemployment
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official labor-market release with specific employment outcomes and age-group breakdown.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Xi because employment outcomes and youth distress were national policy issues under his rule.
contrary_evidence: Total job creation was strong even though youth unemployment remained elevated.

evidence.claim: The PBC said it cut reserve requirements twice, released more than 1 trillion yuan of long-term funds, used multiple liquidity tools, cut benchmark lending rates, expanded policy-bank credit, and supported property-sector rescue measures in 2022.
evidence.title: 2022年第四季度中国货币政策执行报告
evidence.excerpt: The PBC said it cut reserve requirements twice, released more than 1 trillion yuan of long-term funds, used multiple liquidity tools, cut benchmark lending rates, expanded policy-bank credit, and supported property-sector rescue measures in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Central-bank report stating the year's policy actions and monetary conditions in detail.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the 2022 policy response, published immediately after year-end.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Xi because the report describes the macroeconomic stabilization toolkit deployed under the Party-state leadership he headed.
contrary_evidence: The report is self-assessment from the central bank and not an independent audit of effectiveness.

unresolved_gaps: Direct command-and-control, custody, and launch-discipline evidence is still thin.
Concrete arms-control follow-through beyond declaratory no-first-use language is limited.
Crisis de-escalation evidence in the Taiwan and Russia-Ukraine settings is mostly indirect.
Direct evidence of Xi personally authorizing or restraining specific military moves is thin.
Civilian-protection and operational-conduct evidence during the Taiwan crisis is limited.
Evidence of actual mediation or de-escalation in Russia-Ukraine remains mostly declaratory.
Water, sanitation, and local service-variation evidence is thin compared with health, pensions, housing, and crisis response.
Chain-of-command evidence for specific repression episodes remains limited.
Independent evidence on courts, legislatures, and oversight bodies resisting capture is thin.
Succession and term-limit mechanics could be more directly documented as a de facto transfer-rule breach.
Independent evaluation of implementation quality across provinces and local-government debt stress remains limited.
Distributional evidence beyond averages and poverty-lifted subgroups could be stronger.
Water/sanitation and housing-quality evidence is thinner than health, pensions, and child-welfare evidence.
Independent evaluation of service quality, regional equity, and front-line delivery remains limited.
Direct, ruler-specific evidence on Xi's own assets, gifts, family business interests, or beneficial ownership is missing.
Independent findings on concealment or obstruction tied personally to Xi are absent.
Evidence of truthful correction versus rhetorical anti-corruption messaging is weak.
Independent evaluation of whether loyalist-heavy appointments improved competence or mainly tightened political control is thin.
More subnational evidence on execution quality and correction would strengthen the adaptation story.
Durable causal impact of the COVID rollback and economic stabilization package remains under-audited.
